findings.explanation: Following root .gitmodules to data/raw_eyegaze reveals the machine-local source URL. Partial is defensible for the explicitly recursive boundary, while the paper consumes curated files already inside the linked dataset. The assessment correctly avoids claiming those direct inputs are missing.

The three direct module mount points and frozen revisions support inclusion. The transitive source URL is not portable to an independent clone, supporting partial without any live retrieval experiment. This does not establish failure of the direct curated-data retrieval route.

The root links REMoDNaV and installs scientific/rendering packages in its image; the labels module also links REMoDNaV. This supports the software inclusion property. Completeness and historical versions of the linked execution environment remain separate limitations under must/010 and must/015.

The frozen Git inventory records source, manuscript, instructions and configuration as versioned blobs. A deliberately incomplete evidence worktree is not evidence that the original object lacks version control; overriding tree cleanliness is appropriate for this particular item.

The root manifest and inventory identify multi-gigabyte image content through annex pointers, and studyforrest documents and inventories annex-managed recordings. Git identities also cover the Anderson input blobs. Missing payload bytes do not defeat this versioning property.

The root run records container/image as an extra input, whereas the linked labels run identifies only a shell command and raw-data inputs. Partial follows directly from this contrast. The omission of quality_stats from the CLI is also real, but exact-environment linkage, rather than a heuristic derived-file count, is the criterion here.

The root README promises recomputation of every numerical value and all figure SVGs. Its -s -f -r -m route never calls quality_stats, which stores the loss values used in the manuscript and generates velhist.svg. The linked README additionally describes a different pipeline from its recorded run. Native verdict rule 10 caps conflicting documented/mechanical routes at partial; presence of instructions alone cannot support met.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial and identify the omitted quality-statistics/velocity-histogram route and the stale linked instructions. Keep the explicitly disclosed old-versus-container migration separate from these undisclosed gaps.

findings.explanation: The named starting point is real, but it does not implement the reproduction coverage the README promises. quality_stats writes img/velhist.svg and is absent from every CLI dispatch branch; main.tex includes its PDF. Native rule 10 requires partial for this documented-route mismatch even though most results have an executable entry point.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial; specify which results the entry point recomputes and which require an additional procedure. Do not infer complete coverage from a historical exit-zero record.

findings.explanation: The linked Condor generator embeds a personal initial directory and a fixed Python executable. These are actual host execution settings, unlike the Dockerfile cleanup paths and README prompt examples. Partial correctly distinguishes portable root scripts from retained linked scripts.

The image recipe supplies the paper analysis dependencies, while compute_all inherits an unspecified Python/package environment. The linked setup.py lists dependencies but leaves their versions open. Partial is supported by a concrete linked execution route, not merely by failure to locate a preferred lockfile.

The root describes host platforms and Docker compatibility. The linked generator inherits environment variables and assumes a personal working directory and Python 2.7. The adapter also assumes usable non-root Docker access. These inspected assumptions support partial.

Root requirements are discoverable and detailed, but following the labels README leads to Condor-era steps rather than a requirements list for the recorded module execution. This supports partial at the stated recursive scope.

Both the archived environment metadata and linked dependency declarations are committed with code. This item concerns tracking of specifications; their incomplete coverage and floating dependency versions can coexist with met here.

The build/save command is a concrete executable maintenance procedure, and a later committed conversion actually replaces the archived representation to address Docker compatibility. This is more than a one-time specification declaration. The identical should/008 answer and duplicate flags are appropriate.

The root archived image really is content-pinned: the adapter derives and runs its config SHA256, so remodnav:latest in archive metadata is not a floating execution selector. However, the assessment includes linked label generation in scope elsewhere, and that route has an inherited Python environment plus unversioned NumPy/SciPy/statsmodels/matplotlib requirements. Root image identity does not establish an exactly replicable environment for that component.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial for the declared recursive scope, preserving the positive root-image finding and citing the linked environment gap already acknowledged under must/006 and must/010.

findings.explanation: The frozen source and annex web records demonstrate publication metadata and exact artifact identities, not present-day payload accessibility. Not-checked is defensible for accessibility of the complete archived environment under the explicit no-network/no-acquisition boundary; it should not be presented as an observed failure.

The root does document obtaining and selecting its archived environment. The all-object met judgment nevertheless omits the linked labels route: its README does not explain the recorded compute_all environment or how to obtain it. This is the same scope included in the assessment own must/010 and must/012 partial judgments.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for root documentation present but linked environment reproduction undocumented, or explicitly narrow and consistently justify the assessment boundary before claiming met.

findings.explanation: All discovered components are selected by Git identities, with annex extending the same repository mechanism for larger content. No alternative version-control system is required by the inspected composition.

Tool-level CI defines automated package tests, and the paper has historical maintenance execution. Neither checks all current paper instructions regularly. Partial gives credit for the component mechanism while retaining the study-wide gap; the workflow definition is not proof of a newly observed successful CI run.

The tree separates input datasets, reusable code, environment archive and paper outputs. Directory separation alongside subdatasets is relevant native evidence; an environment and generated macros need not each be separate repositories.

The recorded root analysis exit zero and the adapter implementation together establish historical execution through a newly created disposable Docker container. That is equivalent evidence permitted by the instrument. It supports the historical tested pipeline, not a new independent rerun or coverage of omitted quality_stats and every upstream computation.

The Docker adapter creates a container per call and removes it, but the labels run invokes Python directly without constructing an isolated environment. Partial is appropriate across those two execution mechanisms.

The conversion record explicitly runs exit 0 inside the loaded image and the analysis record exercises the archived environment. These are historical maintenance checks; the tool CI installs its own development dependencies and does not regularly reconstitute the paper image. Partial is a reasonable account of that limited coverage.

Image configuration/layer paths are part of the versioned research object, and the frozen inventory records their annex identities. Archival inclusion is distinct from whether this inspection package contains the bytes or whether remote retrieval works today.

The same executable build/save and subsequent recorded maintenance instance support this duplicated criterion. Its upstream-duplicate flag and parity with must/014 prevent treating the duplicate as independent evidence.

The raw-data declaration explicitly says unrestricted access, and Anderson documents released data while noting omitted copyrighted stimuli. No restricted component required by the declared paper computation was identified. N/A on an empty restricted-component subject is justified; it is not a claim that every external stimulus is redistributable.

Root and linked Git module declarations explicitly compose raw data, labels, software and evaluation inputs. This structural property holds independently of the separately reported unresolved source URL.

Root instructions explain the analysis/environment relationship, while the labels reproduction text does not describe its actual current code-module route. Partial is supported by this concrete documentation gap.

Pinned Git module boundaries permit independent component version changes. The cited dependency drift and stale instructions demonstrate environment/actionability problems, but do not by themselves identify a defective modular boundary or an update crossing it. The partial judgment needs a specific coupling or incompatible module-update example.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify which independent module update necessarily breaks the composed workflow and how the boundary causes it, or judge the existing pinned boundaries on their structural evidence without reusing documentation deficiencies as modularity evidence.

findings.explanation: Gitlinks provide the composition mechanism, the container registration binds the environment, and the run record declares input/output relationships. All are directly discoverable from the root and sufficient for this mechanism-oriented item.

Root documentation and module paths provide useful navigation, but the linked README sends users to a superseded mechanism. Partial recognizes the navigation support without implying that the linked execution route is adequately explained.

limitations: Inspection only: no network calls, payload acquisition, scientific workflow execution, container builds, or live issue/CI checks. Missing binary/annex content is an evidence-package limitation, not an observed retrieval failure.

Used only the assigned anonymized response, pinned native instrument and frozen evidence corpus. Material source claims were checked against root-linked files, metadata and cited historical commit records; historical exit values were not independently rerun.
All Git reads used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. One git-show read encountered an intentionally absent blob; its cited commit message was subsequently inspected successfully with cat-file without fetching.

The original probe-output/report files were outside the authorized review input and were not inspected. Probe-related explanations were checked against available helper source and object evidence, not against an independent replay of the original probe invocation.

The native pin check and response validator pass. All 31 native IDs are present: 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY. Response counts are MUST 9 met/7 partial/1 not-checked, SHOULD 5 met/3 partial/1 not-applicable, MAY 2 met/3 partial. No aggregate assessment score is supplied; no hidden report denominator was audited.

Adapter source is cited through its frozen relative locator and SHA256 because the supplied public source locator uses a release tag rather than an immutable commit. Discovery is root README version reference to the registered adapter.
No actual runtime model identity was available as evidence; model_observed remains null. Agreement findings are independent review judgments, not human approval.
